questions.question: For a very dilute solute present in trace quantities, concentration in parts per million (ppm) is defined as:
options: A) \( \frac{\text{Mass of component}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 10^3 \)
B) \( \frac{\text{Moles of component}}{\text{Total volume of solution (L)}} \times 10^6 \)
C) \( \frac{\text{Mass of component}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 10^6 \)
D) \( \frac{\text{Mass of component}}{\text{Mass of solvent}} \times 10^4 \)
questions.explanation: Parts per million (ppm) is defined as \( \frac{\text{Mass of component}}{\text{Total mass of solution}} \times 10^6 \), commonly used for water pollutants and atmospheric contaminants.

questions.sub_topic: Vapour Pressure of Pure Liquid Factors
questions.question: The saturated vapour pressure of a pure liquid depends exclusively on:
options: A) The surface area of the container
B) The total volume of the liquid phase
C) The nature of the liquid and the temperature
D) The atmospheric pressure outside the closed container
questions.explanation: Vapour pressure in a closed container is an intensive thermodynamic equilibrium property determined only by intermolecular forces (nature of liquid) and temperature.

questions.question: When acetic acid is dissolved in benzene, it dimerizes via hydrogen bonding. In this solution, the experimentally observed molar mass of acetic acid will be:
options: A) Half of its normal molar mass, with \( i \approx 2.0 \)
B) Nearly double its normal molar mass, with \( i \approx 0.5 \)
C) Exactly equal to 60 g/mol under all conditions
D) Zero due to complete precipitation
questions.explanation: Due to dimerization (\( 2\ce{CH3COOH <=> (CH3COOH)2} \)), the effective number of particles halves, making colligative properties half of normal and observed molar mass approximately 120 g/mol (double).

questions.question: A binary solution of ethanol and water containing 95.4% ethanol by volume forms a minimum boiling azeotrope because it shows:
options: A) A large negative deviation from Raoult's law
B) Strict adherence to Raoult's law over all compositions
C) Zero vapour pressure at its boiling temperature
D) A large positive deviation from Raoult's law
questions.explanation: Solutions showing large positive deviations from Raoult's law have maximum total vapour pressure at a specific composition, and hence boil at a temperature lower than either pure component (minimum boiling azeotrope).

questions.sub_topic: Degree of Dissociation Calculation from i
questions.question: A 0.1 m aqueous solution of a monobasic weak acid \( \ce{HA} \) freezes at -0.205°C (\( K_f \) of water = 1.86 K kg/mol). The degree of dissociation (\( \alpha \)) of the acid is:
questions.explanation: \( \Delta T_f = i K_f m \Rightarrow 0.205 = i \times 1.86 \times 0.1 = 0.186 i \Rightarrow i = \frac{0.205}{0.186} \approx 1.10 \). For \( \ce{HA <=> H+ + A-} \), \( i = 1 + \alpha \Rightarrow \alpha = i - 1 = 0.10 \) (10%).

questions.question: In the standard Daniell cell operating at 298 K, the overall cell reaction that generates electric current is:
questions.explanation: Zinc has a lower reduction potential (-0.76 V) than copper (+0.34 V), so zinc undergoes oxidation at the anode while copper ions are reduced at the cathode.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary function of the salt bridge in an electrochemical galvanic cell?
options: A) It speeds up the rate of metallic electron transfer along the wire
B) It increases the standard reduction potential of the cathode
C) It maintains electrical neutrality in the two half-cell solutions and completes the internal circuit
D) It completely prevents any ionic motion between half-cells
questions.explanation: A salt bridge allows migration of inert ions (e.g. \( \ce{K+} \) and \( \ce{NO3^-} \)) to neutralize excess charge in both compartments without mechanical mixing of solutions.

questions.question: Upon dilution of an electrolytic solution, how do specific conductance (conductivity, \( \kappa \)) and molar conductivity (\( \Lambda_m \)) vary?
options: A) \( \kappa \) decreases, whereas \( \Lambda_m \) increases
B) Both \( \kappa \) and \( \Lambda_m \) increase
C) Both \( \kappa \) and \( \Lambda_m \) decrease
D) \( \kappa \) increases, whereas \( \Lambda_m \) decreases
questions.explanation: Conductivity (\( \kappa \)) is conductance per unit volume; on dilution, the number of current-carrying ions per unit volume decreases, so \( \kappa \) decreases. Molar conductivity \( \Lambda_m = \kappa / c \) increases because volume increases more than \( \kappa \) decreases.

questions.sub_topic: Equilibrium Constant from Standard Cell Potential
questions.question: The equilibrium constant (\( K_c \)) for a cell reaction at 298 K with \( n=2 \) and \( E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.10 \text{ V} \) is related by:
options: B) \( \log K_c = 2 \times 1.10 \times 0.059 \)
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, \( E_{\text{cell}} = 0 \Rightarrow E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = \frac{0.059}{n} \log K_c \Rightarrow \log K_c = \frac{n E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.059} = \frac{2 \times 1.10}{0.059} \).

questions.question: Galvanization protects iron structures from corrosion even when the surface coating is scratched because:
options: A) Iron atoms evaporate as gaseous hydrides at the scratch boundary
B) Zinc has a more negative reduction potential than iron (\( E^\circ_{\ce{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -0.76\text{ V} < E^\circ_{\ce{Fe^{2+}/Fe}} = -0.44\text{ V} \)) and is preferentially oxidized
C) Zinc forms a diamond-like covalent covalent lattice with atmospheric oxygen
D) Iron acts as the anode while zinc acts as the cathode
questions.explanation: Zinc has a lower reduction potential than iron, so even when damaged, zinc undergoes sacrificial oxidation, protecting the underlying iron cathodically.

questions.sub_topic: Pseudo First Order Example: Ester Hydrolysis
questions.question: The acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of ethyl acetate (\( \ce{CH3COOC2H5 + H2O ->[H+] CH3COOH + C2H5OH} \)) is an example of:
options: A) Zero-order reaction
B) Second-order reaction
C) Pseudo first-order reaction
D) Third-order reaction
questions.explanation: Water is present in large excess, so its concentration remains practically constant throughout the reaction, reducing the bimolecular reaction to pseudo first order: \( \text{Rate} = k'[\ce{CH3COOC2H5}] \).

questions.sub_topic: Effect of Catalyst on Equilibrium Constant
questions.question: What is the effect of adding a catalyst on the value of the equilibrium constant (\( K_{\text{eq}} \)) of a reversible reaction?
options: A) It has no effect on the equilibrium constant
B) It increases the equilibrium constant
C) It decreases the equilibrium constant
D) It inverts the value of the equilibrium constant
questions.explanation: A catalyst increases the rates of forward and reverse reactions equally by lowering the activation barrier for both directions, leaving \( K_{\text{eq}} = k_f / k_b \) unchanged.

questions.sub_topic: Slope of ln k vs 1/T Plot
questions.question: According to the logarithmic Arrhenius equation, a linear plot of \( \ln k \) versus \( 1/T \) gives a straight line with slope equal to:
options: A) \( -\frac{E_a}{R} \)
B) \( +\frac{E_a}{R} \)
C) \( -\frac{R}{E_a} \)
questions.explanation: Taking natural logs of \( k = A e^{-E_a/(RT)} \) yields \( \ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{R} \left(\frac{1}{T}\right) \), which is a straight line \( y = c + mx \) with slope \( m = -E_a/R \).

questions.sub_topic: Time for 75% Completion in First Order
questions.question: For a first-order chemical reaction, the time required for 75% completion (\( t_{75\%} \)) is related to its half-life (\( t_{1/2} \)) by:
questions.explanation: After 1 half-life, 50% remains; after 2 half-lives, 25% remains (75% completed). Thus \( t_{75\%} = 2 t_{1/2} \).

questions.question: In modified collision theory, the rate equation is expressed as \( k = P \cdot Z_{AB} \cdot e^{-E_a / (RT)} \). The factor \( P \) is called:
options: A) Partial pressure factor of reactant vapours
B) Partition function ratio of solvent molecules
C) Steric or probability factor, accounting for proper orientation of colliding molecules
D) Polarization parameter of transitioning orbitals
questions.explanation: The factor \( P \) (steric or orientation factor) takes into account that reacting molecules must collide with proper spatial orientation for bonds to break and form.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.sub_topic: High Enthalpy of Atomization of Transition Metals
questions.question: Transition metals possess high melting points and high enthalpies of atomization primarily because:
options: A) Unpaired (n-1)d electrons together with ns electrons participate extensively in strong metallic bonding
B) They exist as discrete diatomic covalent gas molecules
C) Their outermost s-electrons form hydrogen bonds in the crystal lattice
D) They have very large ionic radii that minimize lattice repulsion
questions.explanation: The participation of both \( ns \) electrons and unpaired \( (n-1)d \) electrons in interatomic metallic bonding creates exceptionally strong cohesive lattice forces.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: Which of the following properties is characteristic of interstitial compounds formed by transition metals with small atoms (H, C, N)?
options: A) They are soft and have very low melting points
B) They act as electrical insulators in solid state
C) They are chemically highly reactive and soluble in water
D) They are very hard and retain metallic electrical conductivity
questions.explanation: Interstitial compounds have high melting points, extreme hardness, retain metallic conductivity, and are chemically relatively inert.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: The steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii along the lanthanoid series (lanthanoid contraction) is attributed to:
options: A) Strong shielding offered by diffuse 5d electrons
B) Imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another in the same subshell
C) Expansion of 6s orbitals with increasing atomic number
D) Decreasing effective nuclear charge across the series
questions.explanation: The 4f orbitals are diffuse and have poor shielding efficiency. With increasing atomic number, effective nuclear charge increases steadily, pulling electrons inward.

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.sub_topic: Standard Reduction Potential Trend in 3d Series
questions.question: In the 3d transition series, copper is the only metal having a positive standard reduction potential (\( E^\circ_{\ce{Cu^{2+}/Cu}} = +0.34 \text{ V} \)). This is because:
options: A) High enthalpy of atomization and sum of first two ionization enthalpies are not compensated by hydration enthalpy
B) Copper has zero enthalpy of atomization
C) Copper ion has an exceptionally large negative hydration enthalpy
D) Copper readily displaces hydrogen gas from dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: The large energy required to transform \( \ce{Cu(s)} \) to \( \ce{Cu^{2+}(aq)} \) (sublimation + ionization) exceeds its hydration enthalpy, resulting in \( E^\circ > 0 \).

questions.topic: Unit IV: d and f Block Elements
questions.question: Mischmetal, a commercially well-known alloy used in flint lighters and cigarette lighters, typically consists of:
options: A) 90% titanium and 10% vanadium
B) About 95% lanthanoid metals (chiefly cerium), ~5% iron, and traces of S, C, Ca, Al
C) 70% copper and 30% zinc
D) 99% mercury and 1% sodium
questions.explanation: Mischmetal consists of lanthanoid metal (~95%, mostly cerium ~40% and lanthanum/neodymium) and iron (~5%), with trace quantities of S, C, Ca, and Al.

questions.question: The ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion (\( \ce{EDTA^{4-}} \)) is an important chelating agent with a denticity of:
options: A) 2 (bidentate)
B) 4 (tetradentate)
C) 8 (octadentate)
D) 6 (hexadentate)
questions.explanation: \( \ce{EDTA^{4-}} \) binds through two nitrogen donor atoms and four carboxylate oxygen donor atoms, making it a hexadentate ligand.

questions.sub_topic: Werner's Theory: Primary and Secondary Valencies
questions.question: According to Alfred Werner's theory of coordination compounds, secondary valencies correspond to:
options: A) The coordination number, and they are directional and non-ionizable
B) The oxidation state, and they are non-directional and ionizable
C) The total electric charge on the outer coordination sphere
D) The number of unpaired d-electrons in the metal atom
questions.explanation: Werner postulated two types of valency: primary (ionizable, satisfies oxidation state) and secondary (non-ionizable, directional in space, satisfies coordination number).

questions.sub_topic: Geometrical Isomerism in Square Planar Complexes
questions.question: Which of the following square planar complexes exists as cis- and trans- isomers?
questions.explanation: Complexes of type \( [\ce{MA2B2}] \) exhibit geometrical isomerism: cis (identical ligands adjacent) and trans (identical ligands opposite at 180°).

questions.question: The complex ion \( [\ce{CoCl4}]^{2-} \) is tetrahedral and has a \( 3d^7 \) configuration with weak-field chloride ligands. Its spin-only magnetic moment is:
options: A) \( \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73 \text{ BM} \)
B) \( \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \text{ BM} \)
C) \( \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83 \text{ BM} \)
D) \( \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90 \text{ BM} \)
questions.explanation: In tetrahedral \( [\ce{CoCl4}]^{2-} \), \( \ce{Co^{2+}} \) is \( d^7 \). Tetrahedral fields are weak, giving electronic configuration \( e^4 t_2^3 \) with \( n=3 \) unpaired electrons: \( \mu = \sqrt{3(5)} = \sqrt{15} = 3.87 \text{ BM} \).

questions.question: Why does the octahedral coordination entity \( [\ce{Co(en)3}]^{3+} \) exhibit optical isomerism (enantiomerism)?
options: A) It lacks a plane or center of symmetry, forming non-superimposable dextro (\( \Delta \)) and laevo (\( \Lambda \)) enantiomers
B) It contains an asymmetric carbon atom inside each ethylenediamine ligand
C) It has four different monodentate ligands bound to the cobalt centre
D) The cobalt atom rotates continuously in opposite directions in solution
questions.explanation: The octahedral chelate complex \( [\ce{M(AA)3}] \) has \( D_3 \) point group symmetry with no improper rotation axes (no plane or inversion centre), rendering it chiral.

questions.question: Among the isomeric butyl bromides, the boiling point decreases in the order:
options: A) tert-Butyl bromide > isobutyl bromide > n-butyl bromide
B) n-Butyl bromide > isobutyl bromide > tert-butyl bromide
C) isobutyl bromide > n-butyl bromide > tert-butyl bromide
D) All isomers have identical boiling points
questions.explanation: With increased branching, the molecule assumes a more spherical shape with smaller surface area, weakening van der Waals forces and lowering the boiling point.

questions.question: Electrophilic chlorination of toluene in the presence of iron(III) chloride catalyst in the dark yields:
options: A) Benzyl chloride exclusively
B) A mixture of o-chlorotoluene and p-chlorotoluene
C) m-Chlorotoluene exclusively
D) Hexachlorocyclohexane
questions.explanation: The methyl group on toluene is ortho- and para-directing due to hyperconjugation and inductive effect, giving a mixture of o- and p-chlorotoluene.

questions.question: When an optically active tertiary alkyl halide undergoes substitution via the \( \text{S}_\text{N}1 \) mechanism, the product is usually:
options: A) A racemic mixture with a slight excess of inverted product due to ion-pair shielding
B) 100% optically pure with complete retention of configuration
C) An optically inactive meso compound without any rotation
D) A cyclic alkene exclusively
questions.explanation: The carbocation intermediate is planar (\( sp^2 \)), so attack can occur from either face; however, the departing leaving group may shield the front face, yielding racemization with partial inversion.

questions.question: The insecticide p,p'-DDT is synthesized by the condensation of chlorobenzene with chloral (\( \ce{CCl3CHO} \)) in the presence of:
options: A) Anhydrous aluminium chloride in carbon disulfide
B) Aqueous potassium hydroxide at room temperature
C) Finely divided nickel catalyst at 200°C
D) Concentrated sulfuric acid (\( \ce{H2SO4} \))
questions.explanation: DDT (2,2-bis(p-chlorophenyl)-1,1,1-trichloroethane) is formed by heating two moles of chlorobenzene with one mole of chloral in conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \).

questions.sub_topic: Influence of Nitro Groups on Chlorobenzene Reactivity
questions.question: Why does the presence of a nitro group at the ortho- or para-position, but NOT at the meta-position, dramatically accelerate nucleophilic aromatic substitution of chlorobenzene?
options: A) The meta-nitro group forms a covalent bond with the incoming hydroxide nucleophile
B) Nitro groups at ortho and para positions cause homolytic C-Cl cleavage
C) The meta position prevents the benzene ring from remaining planar
D) The negative charge in the Meisenheimer carbanion intermediate is directly delocalized onto the electronegative oxygens of the nitro group at ortho and para positions
questions.explanation: In the Meisenheimer intermediate, carbanionic resonance structures place formal negative charge on the ring carbons ortho and para to the leaving group, directly stabilized by the -M effect of the nitro group.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: Acid-catalyzed hydration of propene (\( \ce{CH3-CH=CH2} \)) with water in the presence of dilute \( \ce{H2SO4} \) yields:
options: A) Propan-2-ol
B) Propan-1-ol
C) Propanoic acid
D) 1,2-Propanediol
questions.explanation: Electrophilic addition of \( \ce{H+} \) generates the more stable secondary carbocation (Markovnikov's rule), which is attacked by water to give propan-2-ol.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Oxidation of Primary Alcohols with PCC
questions.question: To selectively oxidize a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without over-oxidation to a carboxylic acid, the reagent of choice is:
options: A) Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) in dichloromethane
B) Acidified potassium permanganate (\( \ce{KMnO4} \))
C) Acidified potassium dichromate (\( \ce{K2Cr2O7} \))
D) Chromic acid in aqueous sulfuric acid (Jones reagent)
questions.explanation: PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) is a mild reagent that stops oxidation at the aldehyde stage because water is absent, preventing hydrate formation.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.question: In the Fischer esterification between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid, water is removed continuously as it forms to:
options: A) Prevent the carboxylic acid from evaporating as a gas
B) Shift the chemical equilibrium towards the ester according to Le Chatelier's principle
C) Lower the temperature of the boiling reaction mixture
D) Neutralize the sulfuric acid catalyst
questions.explanation: Esterification is a reversible reaction with \( K \approx 4 \). Removing water drives the position of equilibrium towards product formation (ester).

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Nitration of Phenol to Picric Acid
questions.question: Heating phenol with concentrated nitric acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid yields:
options: A) o-Nitrophenol only
B) 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid)
C) p-Nitrophenol only
D) 1,3,5-Trinitrobenzene
questions.explanation: Vigorous nitration of phenol with conc. \( \ce{HNO3} \) and conc. \( \ce{H2SO4} \) produces 2,4,6-trinitrophenol, commonly known as picric acid.

questions.topic: Unit VII: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
questions.sub_topic: Cleavage of tert-Butyl Alkyl Ethers with HI
questions.question: Reaction of tert-butyl methyl ether with one equivalent of hydroiodic acid (HI) yields tert-butyl iodide and methanol because:
options: A) Iodide ion attacks the bulky tert-butyl group via an \( \text{S}_\text{N}2 \) pathway
B) The protonated ether dissociates via an \( \text{S}_\text{N}1 \) pathway to form the highly stable tert-butyl carbocation
C) Methanol has a higher boiling point than tert-butyl alcohol
D) The methyl group is a better leaving group than iodide
questions.explanation: When one alkyl group is tertiary, protonation is followed by C-O cleavage generating the stable 3° carbocation (\( \text{S}_\text{N}1 \)), which then combines with \( \ce{I^-} \) to give tert-butyl iodide.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: The Stephen reaction converts nitriles into aldehydes using which reducing agent followed by hydrolysis?
options: A) Zinc and acetic acid
B) Lithium aluminium hydride
C) Tin(II) chloride and hydrochloric acid (\( \ce{SnCl2 + HCl} \))
D) Sodium amalgam and water
questions.explanation: In Stephen reaction, \( \ce{R-CN} \) is reduced with \( \ce{SnCl2 + HCl} \) to an imine hydrochloride (\( \ce{R-CH=NH.HCl} \)), which on boiling with water hydrolyzes to aldehyde.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: Addition of hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to an aldehyde in the presence of a base yields:
options: A) Oxime
B) Cyanohydrin
C) Hydrazone
D) Hemiacetal
questions.explanation: Base generates the nucleophile \( \ce{CN^-} \), which attacks the carbonyl carbon to form a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate, protonated to give a cyanohydrin (\( \ce{R-CH(OH)CN} \)).

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: Which of the following carbonyl compounds will undergo self-aldol condensation in the presence of dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide?
options: A) Methanal (formaldehyde)
B) Benzaldehyde
C) 2,2-Dimethylpropanal (pivalaldehyde)
D) Ethanal (acetaldehyde)
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation requires at least one \( \alpha \)-hydrogen atom to form the nucleophilic enolate ion. Ethanal has three \( \alpha \)-hydrogens, whereas methanal, benzaldehyde, and pivalaldehyde have none.

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.sub_topic: Relative Acidity: Chloroacetic Acid vs Acetic Acid
questions.question: Monochloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid because:
options: A) Chlorine releases electrons into the carbonyl group via +I effect
B) Acetic acid has a higher molecular weight
C) The electron-withdrawing inductive (-I) effect of chlorine disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate anion
D) Monochloroacetic acid has higher volatility
questions.explanation: The electronegative chlorine atom exerts a -I effect, withdrawing electron density through sigma bonds, stabilizing the conjugate base \( \ce{Cl-CH2-COO^-} \).

questions.topic: Unit VIII: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
questions.question: In the Wolff-Kishner reduction, a hydrazone formed from a carbonyl compound is heated with \( \ce{KOH} \) in a high-boiling solvent like ethylene glycol to evolve:
options: A) Ammonia gas (\( \ce{NH3} \)) and generate an alcohol
B) Carbon dioxide (\( \ce{CO2} \)) and generate an alkyne
C) Nitrogen gas (\( \ce{N2} \)) and generate an alkane
D) Hydrogen cyanide (\( \ce{HCN} \)) and generate an amine
questions.explanation: The hydrazone undergoes base-catalyzed deprotonation and rearrangement in hot ethylene glycol, releasing thermodynamically stable \( \ce{N2} \) gas and producing the corresponding alkane.

questions.question: Nitrobenzene is converted to aniline in the laboratory using which reducing combination?
options: A) Sodium hydroxide and hydrogen peroxide
B) Copper sulfate and nitric acid
C) Iron scrap and hydrochloric acid (\( \ce{Fe + HCl} \))
D) Potassium permanganate and sulfuric acid
questions.explanation: \( \ce{Fe + HCl} \) is preferred industrially because \( \ce{FeCl2} \) formed gets hydrolyzed to release \( \ce{HCl} \), requiring only a small catalytic amount of hydrochloric acid.

questions.question: The conversion of benzenediazonium chloride into chlorobenzene using cuprous chloride in hydrochloric acid is called:
options: A) Gattermann reaction
B) Wurtz reaction
C) Balz-Schiemann reaction
D) Sandmeyer reaction
questions.explanation: The replacement of diazonium group by chlorine or bromine using cuprous halide (\( \ce{Cu2Cl2/HCl} \) or \( \ce{Cu2Br2/HBr} \)) is the Sandmeyer reaction.

questions.question: Sulphanilic acid prepared by heating aniline with concentrated sulfuric acid at 453–473 K exists predominantly as a:
options: A) Free neutral amine without ionic charges
B) Zwitterion (\( \ce{^+H3N-C6H4-SO3^-} \))
C) Volatile covalent liquid
D) Dimeric cyclic anhydride
questions.explanation: Sulphanilic acid contains both acidic (\( \ce{-SO3H} \)) and basic (\( \ce{-NH2} \)) groups within the same molecule, undergoing internal proton transfer to form a dipolar zwitterion.

questions.question: Fluorobenzene is conveniently prepared from benzenediazonium chloride by:
options: A) Direct reaction with fluorine gas in the dark
B) Reaction with sodium fluoride and copper powder
C) Precipitating benzenediazonium fluoroborate (\( \ce{ArN2+BF4^-} \)) followed by dry thermal decomposition
D) Heating with concentrated aqueous hydrofluoric acid
questions.explanation: The Balz-Schiemann reaction treats diazonium chloride with \( \ce{HBF4} \) to precipitate \( \ce{ArN2+BF4^-} \), which on dry heating smoothly decomposes into fluorobenzene, \( \ce{BF3} \), and \( \ce{N2} \).

questions.sub_topic: Separation of Amines with Hinsberg Reagent
questions.question: A mixture of 1°, 2°, and 3° amines was treated with benzenesulfonyl chloride and aqueous \( \ce{KOH} \). The resulting sulfonamide from the primary amine:
options: A) Dissolves in aqueous KOH because it contains an acidic hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen
B) Remains insoluble in KOH because it lacks acidic hydrogen atoms
C) Hydrolyzes instantly back to ammonia gas
D) Forms an insoluble crystalline salt with potassium
questions.explanation: Primary amine gives \( \ce{C6H5SO2NHR} \); the hydrogen attached to nitrogen is strongly acidic due to the electron-withdrawing sulfonyl group, dissolving in alkali as a potassium salt.

questions.question: Amino acids that cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be supplied through diet are known as:
options: A) Non-essential amino acids
B) Acidic amino acids
C) Basic amino acids
D) Essential amino acids
questions.explanation: Essential amino acids (e.g. valine, leucine, lysine) cannot be manufactured in human metabolic pathways and must be obtained from dietary sources.

questions.question: Keratin (found in hair, wool, and nails) and myosin (found in muscles) are classified as:
options: A) Globular proteins, which are soluble in water
B) Phospholipids, which form membrane bilayers
C) Oligosaccharides, which act as cell antigens
D) Fibrous proteins, which are insoluble in water
questions.explanation: In fibrous proteins, polypeptide chains run parallel and are held together by hydrogen and disulfide bonds, forming rope-like fiber structures that are insoluble in water.

questions.question: Which of the following nitrogenous bases is found in RNA but is absent in DNA?
options: A) Thymine
B) Uracil
C) Cytosine
D) Adenine
questions.explanation: RNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and uracil. DNA contains adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine (uracil is absent in DNA).

questions.question: Amylopectin, the water-insoluble fraction of starch, is a branched-chain polymer of \( \alpha \)-D-glucose with branching occurring via:
options: A) \( \alpha \)-(1,4)-glycosidic linkages only
B) \( \beta \)-(1,4)-glycosidic linkages
C) \( \alpha \)-(1,6)-glycosidic linkages
D) \( \beta \)-(1,6)-glycosidic linkages
questions.explanation: Amylopectin chains are composed of \( \alpha \)-D-glucose linked by \( \alpha \)-(1,4) bonds, with branching points formed by \( \alpha \)-(1,6) glycosidic linkages at intervals of 20-30 units.

questions.question: The regular folding patterns in the secondary structure of proteins (\( \alpha \)-helix and \( \beta \)-pleated sheet) are stabilized by:
options: A) Hydrogen bonds between the C=O of one peptide bond and the N-H of another
B) Covalent ester linkages between side chains
C) Phosphodiester bonds connecting alpha-carbons
D) Ionic coordination with magnesium ions
questions.explanation: The secondary structure arises exclusively from hydrogen bonding between the carbonyl oxygen (\( \ce{>C=O} \)) and the amino hydrogen (\( \ce{-NH-} \)) of the polypeptide backbone.
